newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay Central Bank shuts Banco Union for 5 days.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay Central Bank shuts Banco Union for 5 days.

text.p: Paraguay's Central Bank said Banco Union, the country's largest private nationally-owned bank, will be closed for five days from Monday to determine the size of a capital injection shareholders must pledge.
The Central Bank said in a press release it "will determine the necessary capital for shareholders to pledge during a shareholders meeting to be called to that end."
Earlier today, the central bank took control of the Union due to liquidity problems.
An official source who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity said Union would need an injection of $260 million.
The Central Bank said it "will honor savers' deposits within the limits established by law." Local law establishes an official guarantee on deposits up to some $2,300.
With some $190 million in deposits, the bank is Paraguay's third largest holder of public deposits, and the biggest in private corporate deposits.
Last week, authorities took control of Ahorros Paraguayos, a savings and loan institution linked to Banco Union through some of its board members, also due to a lack of liquidity.

Paraguay has been in the grips of a financial crisis since May 1995 which according to official data has required the injection of $500 million in funds. ((-- Jose Maria Amarilla, Asuncion newsroom, 595 21 444527))
